subject: Issue with round_any on POSIXct objects

messages.author: a04fc201bcc65016
messages.subject: Issue with round_any on POSIXct objects
parts:
Hi there:

I got this problem with the function round_any()

Sys.time()
[1] "2014-07-27 06:45:17 COT"

round_any(Sys.time(),60)
[1] "2014-07-27 11:45:00 COT"

As you see it doesn't round 60 seconds.

I use plyr version 1.8.1.

Is it an issue with LOCALE?

Thank you for your help.

Kenneth

messages.subject: Re: Issue with round_any on POSIXct objects
parts: When I run your example, I get a timezone warning and returned value in GMT, but the result is corrent. Perhaps take a look at `round_date` in the (amazingly helpful) `lubridate` pacakge. I use that whenever I am doing anything with dates (I didn't realize `round_any` was supposed to work on times!).

messages.subject: Re: Issue with round_any on POSIXct objects
parts:
Thank you Doug for your advice.

I was using round_any() from package plyr because in their help documentation says:

Usage

round_any(x, accuracy, f = round)

Arguments

x
numeric or date-time (POSIXct) vector to round
accuracy
number to round to; for POSIXct objects, a number of seconds
I will use lubridate package.

El domingo, 27 de julio de 2014 15:10:52 UTC-5, Doug Mitarotonda escribió:
When I run your example, I get a timezone warning and returned value in GMT, but the result is corrent. Perhaps take a look at `round_date` in the (amazingly helpful) `lubridate` pacakge. I use that whenever I am doing anything with dates (I didn't realize `round_any` was supposed to work on times!).
